chris: rolled the 'window-cohort' recalibration to canary at 09:12 and immediately saw p99 jump ~2x on s1 pools, overall throughput -18%. seems correlated with small-request mix.
deploy-bot: deploy started by chris (commit 9f4b2a7) -> canary-s1 (3 hosts)
lina: confirm commit + which config keys changed?
chris: commit 9f4b2a7 changed token_budget_target from 120->75 and split_cohort_window from 50->30, also enabled token-smoothing:true
paul: ok that token_budget drop is aggressive. can you paste kernel routing logs for one affected host?
chris: pasted snippet from /var/log/runtime/router.log: ``[09:14:33] route_decision id=0x7f cohort=small -> kernel=fast_small_seq, batch_size=1, reason=token_budget_floor``
roshan: interesting — kernel choice flipped to the single-step fast_small_seq a lot more often. that kernel has higher per-token overhead for batch<4 in our perf matrix.
anya: KV cache hitrate for the canary dropped ~12% around the same time (query: sum(rate(kv_cache_hits[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_lookups[5m]))). could be cohort window change causing prefix misalignment.
chris: attaching quick flame description: cpu on CPU0 shows longer wait on kernel-switch path (mutex contention around batch-coalescer). microprofile shows more frequent calls to pick_kernel_for_shape().
paul: do we have the scheduler metrics? queue_latency distribution?
chris: queue_latency p50 ~4ms -> 6ms, p95 18ms -> 42ms, p99 68ms -> 134ms. token_budget usage per-window shows more fragmentation; effective batch sizes down from 6->2.
lina: can we reproduce locally with a workload that has many short tail requests? perhaps run the canary config on staging and replay production trace.
roshan: also grep kernel logs for "fallback_to_slow_path" — I suspect our kernel-selector is preferring narrow fast kernel when KV cache misses force additional prefill, creating serial work per request.
chris: found lines: ``fallback_to_slow_path=true reason=kv_miss prefill_tokens=16`` repeated. when prefill triggers, token_budget_target small makes batcher avoid waiting for other requests -> serialization.
anya: suggestion: increase token_budget_target back to 110 for canary and cap token-smoothing window to avoid aggressive early flush. that should let batcher gather ~4-8 requests and favor the bigger kernel.
paul: quick mitigation: flip split_cohort_window back to 50 and throttle token-smoothing (set to gentle). prefer targeted rollback on canary hosts.
lina: agreed. chris, can you patch canary config and restart coalescer on the 3 hosts? include debug flags: ``--batcher-verbose --kernel-routing-trace``
chris: prepping patch now. command I'm going to run: ``curl -XPOST http://canary-config/override -d '{"token_budget_target":110,"split_cohort_window":50,"token_smoothing":false}' && systemctl restart runtime-batcher``
deploy-bot: override applied to canary-s1 hosts by chris
chris: rolled overrides, restarting. will monitor.
roshan: meanwhile can we capture an end-to-end trace for one slow request (trace-id) and the kernel selection timeline? add kv cache events to trace.
chris: capturing trace 0a7c... posted link to /traces/0a7c with timeline: kernel_select -> kv_prefill -> wait_for_batch -> execute_kernel_small -> emit. shows waits between kernel_select and execute increased on avg ~40ms.
anya: good find. we should add a guard: if kv_prefill increases expected latency beyond X ms, force fallback to the larger-kernel path to keep throughput. open to making it heuristic: if predicted_prefill_tokens>8 then prefer large kernel.
paul: filing a quick follow-up: create issue to add "prefill-aware kernel preference" and a conservative token_budget floor; also add an alert for sudden kv_hitrate drop >8% in 5m for canary.
chris: monitoring looks better after override: p99 trending down to baseline over 10m, throughput recovering. I'll keep this thread updated and send a postmortem summary once we have full traces.
lina: great. assign owners: chris (rollback + monitor), roshan (trace analysis + spec prefill-aware rule), anya (alert + KV metrics dashboard), paul (follow-up issue + tests).
chris: noted. thanks all :thumbsup:
